body.statement: For every observed mass array \(q\) and budget pair \((\delta_D,\delta_S)\in\mathcal B\), the projection onto \((d,(h_x)_x,(n_x)_x)\) of all laws \(P\in\mathcal M(\delta_D,\delta_S)\) inducing \(q\) is exactly the corresponding projection of \(\bigcup_{o\in\mathcal O}Q_o(q,\delta_D,\delta_S)\). Every full reduced array in every branch \(Q_o\) lifts to a full response law inducing the same \(q\), with the displayed \(h_x\) and \(n_x\). Each fixed branch admits a linear extended formulation with \(O(mK)\) variables, constraints, and nonzero coefficients; its numerical coefficients are rational whenever \(q\), \(\delta_D\), and \(\delta_S\) are rational. At \((\delta_D,\delta_S)=(0,0)\), this result recovers the accepted-bank result \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport/thm:sharp-exact-mass-threshold-interval}\) on the no-defier, covariate-wise one-sided-selection boundary. Beyond that accepted boundary result, the present extension is the positive-budget regime with unknown diagonal residuals and defiers, within-cell coexistence of opposing selection responses, budget-coupled survivor mass, and exact orientation-indexed disjunctive branches; no branch-free scalable positive-budget algorithm is asserted.
body.justification: This is the positive-budget extension kernel: it converts unknown diagonal residuals, treatment defiers, and budget-coupled opposing selection responses into exact orientation-specific branches and proves every reduced point lifts.
body.gap: The accepted \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport\_v1}\) paper already proves the branch-free no-defier, covariate-wise one-sided-selection boundary, including ordinal cuts, full-law lifting, sharp endpoints, and sparse threshold flow. The new result is the positive \(\delta_D\), positive \(\delta_S\) disjunctive projection with within-cell opposing responses and unknown defier residuals.
body.consumer: It makes the positive-budget survivor-complier ordinal-benefit surface exactly computable, branch by branch, for Job Corps and Oregon encouragement designs.
body.proof_tex:
For \(d\in\{0,1\}\), introduce the proof intermediate
\[
 \widetilde V_d=
 \begin{cases}
 Y_d,&S_d=1,\\
 \bot,&S_d=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:receipt\text{-}consistency}\), \(\mathrm{ass:selection\text{-}consistency}\), \(\mathrm{ass:outcome\text{-}consistency}\), \(\mathrm{ass:selection\text{-}exclusion}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:outcome\text{-}exclusion}\), a unit with response vector \(R\) produces \((D_0,\widetilde V_{D_0})\) under \(Z=0\) and \((D_1,\widetilde V_{D_1})\) under \(Z=1\). Conditional randomization in \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}randomization}\) and assignment overlap in \(\mathrm{ass:assignment\text{-}overlap}\) therefore identify, within every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the two margins of this pair as the observed masses \(q^0_{xdw}\) and \(q^1_{xdw}\) from \(\mathrm{def:observed\text{-}masses}\).

For the forward projection, represent a response type in cell \(x\) by an arc from its state under \(Z=0\) to its state under \(Z=1\), with mass \(P(X=x,R=r)\). If \(D_0=D_1=d\), both assignments expose the same treatment-specific state \((d,\widetilde V_d)\), so the arc is diagonal. Let its mass at state \(w\) be \(d_{xdw}\). The two margin equations and nonnegativity give
\[
 0\leq d_{xdw}\leq\min\{q^0_{xdw},q^1_{xdw}\}.
\]
The treatment-zero to treatment-one off-diagonal arcs are precisely compliers, with left and right margins
\[
 u_{xw}=q^0_{x0w}-d_{x0w},
 \qquad
 v_{xw}=q^1_{x1w}-d_{x1w}.
\]
The reverse arcs are precisely defiers. Their treatment-zero and treatment-one state margins are
\[
 r_{xw}=q^1_{x0w}-d_{x0w},
 \qquad
 s_{xw}=q^0_{x1w}-d_{x1w}.
\]
All four residual vectors are nonnegative. Taking table totals yields
\[
 \sum_{w\in\mathcal V}u_{xw}
 =\sum_{w\in\mathcal V}v_{xw}=c_x,
 \qquad
 \sum_{w\in\mathcal V}r_{xw}
 =\sum_{w\in\mathcal V}s_{xw}=f_x,
\]
which are exactly the relations in \(\mathrm{def:diagonal\text{-}residuals}\).

Within the complier table, let \(h_x\) be the mass selected under both treatments. Since the selected row and column masses are \(U_x\) and \(V_x\), the four selection-response masses for \((S_0,S_1)=(1,1),(1,0),(0,1),(0,0)\) are
\[
 h_x,
 \qquad U_x-h_x,
 \qquad V_x-h_x,
 \qquad c_x-U_x-V_x+h_x.
\]
Their nonnegativity is equivalent to
\[
 \max\{0,U_x+V_x-c_x\}
 \leq h_x\leq\min\{U_x,V_x\}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:ordinal\text{-}cuts}\), the selected--selected strict-benefit mass \(n_x\) is characterized exactly by
\[
 0\leq n_x\leq h_x,
 \qquad
 n_x\geq h_x-B_{xk}\quad(-1\leq k\leq K-1),
 \qquad
 n_x\leq G_{xk}\quad(0\leq k\leq K).
\]
Moreover, \(\mathrm{def:selected\text{-}complier\text{-}margins}\) gives
\[
 a_x=U_x-h_x,
 \qquad b_x=V_x-h_x,
 \qquad
 \min\{a_x,b_x\}=\min\{U_x,V_x\}-h_x.
\]
Choose \(o_x=1\) when \(U_x\leq V_x\), and \(o_x=0\) otherwise. Then
\[
 o_xU_x+(1-o_x)V_x-h_x=\min\{a_x,b_x\}.
\]
Thus \(\mathrm{ass:selection\text{-}minority\text{-}budget}\) is exactly the branch budget for this orientation, while \(\mathrm{ass:defier\text{-}budget}\) gives \(\sum_xf_x\leq\delta_D\). Every compatible full law therefore projects into at least one branch \(Q_o\).

For the reverse direction, take a complete reduced array in a fixed \(Q_o(q,\delta_D,\delta_S)\). For every \(x\), \(\mathrm{lem:ordinal\text{-}cuts}\) supplies a selected--selected complier coupling of mass \(h_x\) and benefit mass \(n_x\), together with a completion through \(\bot\) to the full margins \(u_x,v_x\). This constructs the complier arc table.

The defier margins have common total \(f_x\). If \(f_x>0\), define
\[
 \rho_x(w_1,w_0)
 =\frac{s_{xw_1}r_{xw_0}}{f_x},
\]
where \(w_1\) is the treatment-one state exposed under \(Z=0\) and \(w_0\) is the treatment-zero state exposed under \(Z=1\). Division is valid in this case, and direct summation gives margins \(s_x\) and \(r_x\). If \(f_x=0\), nonnegativity and the margin equalities force \(r_x=s_x=0\), and the zero table has the required margins. Adjoin the diagonal arcs of masses \(d_{xdw}\).

Every constructed arc determines a response type. A complier or defier arc specifies both treatment-specific endpoint pairs \((S_0,Y_0)\) and \((S_1,Y_1)\). If an endpoint is \(\bot\), set the corresponding selection response to zero and assign the unobserved potential outcome an arbitrary fixed element of \(\mathcal Y\). A treatment-\(d\) diagonal arc specifies the treatment-\(d\) response; fill the never-exposed treatment-\((1-d)\) response arbitrarily. The arc masses are nonnegative, their arm margins are exactly \(q^0,q^1\), and they total \(p_x\) in cell \(x\) because \(\sum_{d,w}q^z_{xdw}=p_x\). Give \(Z\) any conditional assignment probability strictly between zero and one and draw it independently of \(R\) given \(X\). This enforces conditional randomization and overlap without changing the conditional arm margins. Receipt, selection, and outcome consistency and both exclusions hold by the response-type construction.

The lifted defier mass obeys \(\sum_xf_x\leq\delta_D\). Its actual minority mass satisfies
\[
 \min\{a_x,b_x\}
 =\min\{U_x,V_x\}-h_x
 \leq o_xU_x+(1-o_x)V_x-h_x.
\]
Summing and using the branch inequality gives
\[
 \sum_x\min\{a_x,b_x\}
 \leq\delta_S\sum_xc_x.
\]
Thus the lift lies in \(\mathcal M(\delta_D,\delta_S)\) and has exactly the prescribed \((d,(h_x)_x,(n_x)_x)\). This proves both projection directions.

To keep the causal target distinct from its identifying functional, define within the proof
\[
 \Theta_I^{\rm causal}(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)
 =\left\{
 \Pr_P(Y_1>Y_0\mid C,S_0=S_1=1):
 P\in\mathcal M(\delta_D,\delta_S),
 P\text{ induces }q,
 H(P)>0
 \right\}.
\]
For every such law, the definitions of \(N\) and \(H\) imply
\[
 \Pr_P(Y_1>Y_0\mid C,S_0=S_1=1)=\frac NH.
\]
The two projection directions, rather than a definition of the causal quantity, therefore prove
\[
 \Theta_I^{\rm causal}(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)
 =\Theta_I(q;\delta_D,\delta_S).
\]

For the size claim, introduce per-cell prefixes
\[
 P^u_{x0}=P^v_{x0}=0,
 \qquad
 P^u_{x,k+1}=P^u_{xk}+u_{xk},
 \qquad
 P^v_{x,k+1}=P^v_{xk}+v_{xk}
 \quad(0\leq k\leq K-1).
\]
Then \(U_x=P^u_{xK}\), \(V_x=P^v_{xK}\), and
\[
 B_{xk}=U_x-P^u_{x,k+1}+P^v_{x,k+1}
 \quad(-1\leq k\leq K-1),
\]
with the zero-prefix convention for \(k=-1\), while
\[
 G_{xk}=P^u_{xk}+V_x-P^v_{x,k+1}
 \quad(0\leq k\leq K-1),
 \qquad
 G_{xK}=U_x.
\]
There are \(O(K)\) residual, survivor, benefit, and prefix variables and \(O(K)\) constant-support constraints per cell. Apart from the two global budget rows, all remaining rows also have constant support per outcome category. Hence each fixed orientation branch, and only each branch, has \(O(mK)\) variables, constraints, and nonzero coefficients. Its coefficients are integers or entries of \(q,\delta_D,\delta_S\), so they are rational when those inputs are rational. The union may have up to \(2^m\) branches; no branch-free or scalable \(O(mK)\) positive-budget computation is implied.

At \((\delta_D,\delta_S)=(0,0)\), nonnegativity and \(\sum_xf_x=0\) force \(f_x=0\), hence \(r_x=s_x=0\), in every cell. The residual identities then fix
\[
 d_{x0w}=q^1_{x0w},
 \qquad
 d_{x1w}=q^0_{x1w},
\]
and therefore make \(u_x,v_x,U_x,V_x\) observable. The zero minority budget forces \(\min\{a_x,b_x\}=0\), or equivalently \(h_x=\min\{U_x,V_x\}\), cell by cell. In the reduced union, the nonnegative branch summands likewise force the orientation to choose the smaller margin, up to ties. Thus the orientation disjunction collapses to the branch-free exact-mass survivor-complier partial-transport problem, and \(\mathrm{lem:ordinal\text{-}cuts}\) and the lift above give its ordinal cuts, sharp attained endpoints, and full-law completion.

This zero-budget specialization recovers, and is explicitly credited to, the accepted CausalSmith boundary results \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport/thm:sharp-exact-mass-threshold-interval}\), \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport/thm:full-law-endpoint-attainment}\), and \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport/thm:linear-sparse-threshold-flow}\), specialization \(\mathrm{v1}\). The present extension begins at positive \(\delta_D\) and \(\delta_S\): diagonal residuals and defier margins become unknown, both opposing selection responses may coexist within a cell, survivor mass is coupled through the aggregate minority budget, and the exact projection becomes the orientation-indexed disjunctive union proved above.
